newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shares end lower on political uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Israel shares end lower on political uncertainty.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly lower on Tuesday in very low volume as investors remained on the sidelines amid rising political uncertainty, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 1.58 percent, or 3.91 points, to 243.89 on low all-share turnover of 77 million shekels against 84 million shekels on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.65 percent lower at 250.46.

"The political situation was the dominant factor in trading today. On Monday there were hopes for a breakthrough in the peace talks but now everything looks very gloomy," said a trader at Tachlit Securities.

Israel broke ground on Tuesday for a Jewish neighborhood in Har Homa in Arab East Jerusalem, raising Israeli-PLO tensions, while Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat sprurned Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu appeals to meet him, drawing Israeli accusations he was trying to stoke already high tensions.

"The market fell and the mood is negative. Investors are sitting on the fence waiting to see what will happen with the Har Homa work. If nothing happens I believe that the market will recover on Wednesday," said a trader at Bank Leumi.
"Volume was very low today and the only active players were options speculators. Stock prices are very attractive but the mood is bearish," the Tachlit trader said.
The decline of Israeli shares traded in New York added to the negative mood, the Leumi trader added.

First International Bank of Israel gained 0.5 percent to 236,763 agorot. The bank said on Tuesday that net profit rose in the fourth quarter of 1996 to 42.3 million shekels from 40.3 million at the same period last year.
Clal Electronics fell 2.5 percent to 33,181 agorot after reporting that net profit in 1996 fell to 110.1 million shekels from 129.6 million a year earlier.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which fell 4.0 percent to 19,262 agorot on turnover of 4.0 million shekels; Leumi Insurance Holdings, which lost 1.25 percent to 253 agorot on volume of 3.6 million shekels; and Koor Industries, which fell 1.75 percent to 30,338 agorot on turnover of 2.5 million shekels.

Assicurazioni Generali was due to make a tender offer to Leumi Insurance shareholders at the end of trading today. Gernrali will pay 3.3148 shekels each for the shares for up to 42.2 percent of a single shareholding.
